title: Quadratic Equations: Factoring, Formula, and Parabolas

questions.question: Which of the following is a quadratic equation?
questions.rationale: A quadratic has its unknown to exactly the second power and no higher — x² − 5x + 6 = 0 fits; the others are linear or cubic.

questions.question: Solve by factorising: x² − 5x + 6 = 0
questions.rationale: Two numbers multiplying to +6 and adding to −5 are −2 and −3, so (x−2)(x−3)=0 gives x = 2 or 3.

questions.question: The quadratic formula is:
questions.rationale: The formula subtracts 4ac inside the root and divides everything by 2a: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.

questions.question: If the discriminant D = b² − 4ac equals 0, the equation has:
questions.rationale: D = 0 means the square-root term vanishes, leaving one value x = −b/2a — the parabola just touches the x-axis.

questions.question: For x² + 4x + 4 = 0, what does the graph do at x = −2?
options: Touches the x-axis and turns back
questions.rationale: Here D = 16 − 16 = 0: a double root at x = −b/2a = −2, so the parabola is tangent to the axis there.

questions.question: The discriminant of 2x² − 3x + 5 = 0 is:
questions.rationale: D = (−3)² − 4(2)(5) = 9 − 40 = −31, so there are no real roots.

questions.question: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of the roots equals:
questions.rationale: Sum of roots α + β = −b/a; the product αβ = c/a.

questions.question: If one root of x² − 7x + k = 0 is 3, then k equals:
questions.rationale: Substituting: 9 − 21 + k = 0 → k = 12. (Check via product: other root is 4, and 3 × 4 = 12.)

questions.question: The parabola y = −2x² + x opens:
questions.rationale: Only the sign of a decides direction: a = −2 < 0 means it opens downward and has a maximum.

questions.question: Solve x² = 49.
questions.rationale: Both 7² and (−7)² equal 49, so a squared equation generally yields two solutions: x = ±7.
